corrected_value.authors: Mayshar, J., Moav, O., and Pascali, L.
corrected_value.title: The origin of the state: Land productivity or appropriability?

decisions.quote:
This is a replication of Mayshar et al. (2022) (henceforth MMP).1 The article posits
that the state (defined as societal hierarchy such as tax-levying elites) originated from
cultivation of appropriable cereal grains, contrary to the conventional theory that the
state originated from increased land productivity following the adoption of agriculture.
The article uses multiple datasets to demonstrate a causal effect of cereal cultivation on
hierarchy (Claim 1) without finding a similar effect for land productivity (Claim 2), and
that societies based on roots or tubers display levels of hierarchy similar to nonfarming
societies (Claim 3).
decisions.location: Section 1 Introduction, p. 3, lines 128-135 (and References, p. 22, lines 2130-2131)
decisions.reason: The paper explicitly re-tests Mayshar, J., Moav, O., and Pascali, L. (2022), 'The origin of the state: Land productivity or appropriability?', Journal of Political Economy, 130(4):1091-1144 (lines 2130-2131). The shipped row erroneously entered the metadata of the comment/replication authors and paper itself (Cook; Duprey; Heyes; Pelli, 2026, 'The Origin of the State: Land Productivity or Appropriability? A Comment') as the original study. Blind coding correctly identified Mayshar et al. (2022) as target 0.

decisions.quote:
Table 1 is the result of our computational reproduction of MMP. The results we estimate using the same data and code are almost the same as the published version. Any
discrepancies we have found are presented in red text; these discrepancies are small and
do not change the qualitative interpretation of the results.
decisions.reason: The authors explicitly confirm the computational reproducibility of Mayshar et al. (2022) (lines 184, 447-448) and judge the minor discrepancies in Table 1 (such as an F-statistic of 16.10 vs. 16.11 and a missing decimal typo in a first-stage coefficient) to be small and non-substantive ('do not change the qualitative interpretation of the results'). Under the codebook, negligible numerical differences that the authors treat as non-substantive map to 'computationally reproducible', not 'computational issues'.

decisions.quote:
The computational reproduction of Mayshar et al. (2022) confirms that their data and
code closely reproduce the main results presented in their Table 1. Our robustness replication with a range of plausible alternative specifications points to additional nuance and
sometimes eroded support for the main results.
decisions.reason: Across Tables 2-11, re-analyses of the original Mayshar et al. (2022) dataset using alternative specifications (concurrently including land productivity, recoding the 1-5 hierarchy scale, winsorizing the top 3% of the instrument, and altering sample restrictions on non-farming and tuber-only societies) materially weaken statistical support for Claim 1 and contradict Claim 3. Both shipped and blind correctly coded 'robustness challenges'.

decisions.quote:
The remainder of this replication is dedicated to examining the robustness replicability
of Table 1 of MMP. In other words, answering the question “Does using the same data
provided by the authors but reasonable alternative procedures produce the same (or at
least similar) estimates?”
decisions.location: Section 3 Scope of Robustness Replicability, p. 5, lines 207-210
decisions.reason: The study re-analyses the original data and code from Mayshar et al. (2022) to check computational reproducibility (Section 2, Table 1) and analytical robustness across alternative specifications (Section 3, Tables 2-12) without collecting a new independent sample. Both shipped and blind correctly coded the record type as 'reproduction'.
